topic: BNB Agent Studio — technical surface for third-party agent enumeration and integration (AiKi, BSC chain 56)
executive_summary:
ANSWER FIRST: **No. BNB Chain does not operate a public API, registry service, index or export that enumerates agents created with Agent Studio.** Nothing in docs.bnbchain.org/developer-kit/bnbchain-studio/ (quickstart, demo, architecture, configuration, cli-reference, deployment, security) describes a hosted directory, a REST/GraphQL discovery service, an auth model for one, or a response shape. The launch blog explicitly frames discovery as standards-based, not centralised: "Other agents can discover and call the one you've built." The `bag agents list/show/forget/register` command group exists, but `forget` semantics and the absence of any network endpoint in the docs indicate a **local address book**, not a queryable network registry (unverified — logged as a gap).

The only enumeration substrate is **on-chain**: Agent Studio's `bag erc8004 register` mints into an ERC-8004 IdentityRegistry, an upgradeable ERC-721 with `totalSupply()`, `exists(uint256)`, `getAgentWallet(uint256)` and a per-token `agentURI`. AiKi can therefore enumerate by walking token IDs 1..totalSupply() and resolving each `agentURI` (base64 data-URI JSON carrying `name`, `description`, `protocol`, `endpoint`). The BRC8004 IdentityRegistry on chain 56 is `0xfA09B3397fAC75424422C4D28b1729E3D4f659D7`; I could not verify from a primary source that bnbagent-sdk targets exactly this address, so **verify before building on it**. A third-party alternative exists: The Graph's Agent0 subgraphs index ERC-8004 on BNB Chain (API-key gateway, GraphQL), but the BNB subgraph ID is not published in the announcement.

Architecture is two artifacts: Layer A agent on AWS Bedrock AgentCore (invoke-only, **no public HTTP routes**), Layer B keyless service on EC2/Fargate exposing `POST /apex/negotiate` and `/apex/health`. No `/.well-known`, no A2A AgentCard. Signing policy (price clamp, EIP-712 allowlist) is enforced **in-process, off-chain**.

findings.claim: There is NO BNB-operated public API, registry service, index, or export to enumerate Agent Studio agents.
findings.detail: Across all eight Agent Studio doc pages fetched (index, quickstart, demo, architecture, configuration, cli-reference, deployment, security) no hosted discovery endpoint, base URL, auth scheme or response schema is documented. The demo page states discovery works the other way: a buyer must already hold an `agent_id`, then reads the on-chain ERC-8004 registry for that ID's `agent_uri` to obtain the service endpoint. The launch blog (2026.7.1) says only "Other agents can find it and call it" and attributes discovery to ERC-8004/ERC-8183 standards, never to a BNB-hosted directory. The networks doc declines even to publish contract addresses, deferring to upstream repos — behaviour inconsistent with an operated index service. DEPLOYED status: not observed. MARKETING status: no marketplace claim made. Practical consequence for AiKi: launch supply cannot be seeded by calling a BNB endpoint; it must be derived from chain state (see next finding) or from a third-party indexer.

findings.claim: The viable enumeration path is the ERC-8004 IdentityRegistry ERC-721 on BSC: totalSupply() + per-ID agentURI resolution.
findings.detail: BRC8004 ("Trustless Agents on BNB Chain", ERC-8004 implementation) publishes an upgradeable ERC-721 IdentityRegistry with `register(string agentURI) returns (uint256 agentId)`, `setAgentURI`, `setAgentWallet`, `totalSupply()`, `exists(uint256)`, `getAgentWallet(uint256)`. BSC mainnet (chain 56): IdentityRegistry `0xfA09B3397fAC75424422C4D28b1729E3D4f659D7`, ReputationRegistry `0x17860530385Bdde7992c4Da71B9ec7791E474C08`. Testnet (97) addresses not in that README. AiKi can enumerate by scanning 1..totalSupply() (IDs are sequential from `register`) or by indexing ERC-721 Transfer-from-zero mint events, then resolving each `agentURI`. CAVEAT — the README did not expose `tokenByIndex` or a registration event signature, and I could NOT confirm from a primary bnb-chain source that `bag erc8004 register` writes to this exact address. The official networks page says addresses live in the bnbagent-sdk and apex-contracts repos, not in docs. Treat the address as SPEC-adjacent, verify on BscScan before wiring.

findings.claim: Third-party alternative: The Graph's Agent0 subgraphs index ERC-8004 agents on BNB Chain via GraphQL.
findings.detail: Announced 2026-04-14. Multi-chain ERC-8004 indexing across Ethereum, Base, Polygon, BNB Chain and Monad. Queried through the standard decentralised gateway `https://gateway.thegraph.com/api/<API_KEY>/subgraphs/id/<SUBGRAPH_ID>`. Auth = Subgraph Studio API key in the path. Entities/fields named in the announcement: `agentRegistrationFiles`, `agentId`, `name`, `description`, `mcpEndpoint`, `mcpTools`, `supportedTrusts`. It also claims coverage of reputation scores with full feedback history, validation records and protocol-wide statistics. The BNB-specific SUBGRAPH_ID is NOT published — the post directs readers to search "agent0" on Graph Explorer per network. This is the closest thing to a callable enumeration API for AiKi's launch supply, but it is operated by The Graph/agent0lab, not BNB Chain, and indexes the ERC-8004 registry generally (not "agents made with Studio" specifically). Source repo: github.com/agent0lab/subgraph.

findings.claim: Developer workflow: pip-installed `bag` CLI scaffolds a two-layer project; agent runs on AWS Bedrock AgentCore, service on EC2/Fargate.
findings.detail: Sequence verbatim: `pip install bnbagent-studio` → `bag --version` → `bag skills install` → `bag init weather-seller` → `cd weather-seller` → `bag dev` → `bag deploy prepare` → `bag deploy agent` → `bag deploy verify --endpoint <service-url>`. `bag init` flags: `--framework adk --runtime agentcore --llm-provider pieverse-llm --network bsc-testnet --no-onboard --ide claude-code|cursor|both`. Default framework is Google ADK; default runtime AgentCore; default network bsc-testnet. Local dev mirrors production: Agent on :8080, Service on :8003. Production split — Layer A (agent) thin-wraps `agentcore deploy` onto AWS Bedrock AgentCore; Layer B (service) ships as a zip with `service.py` at top level to EC2 or Fargate. Layer B calls Layer A via AWS `InvokeAgentRuntime` for signing. Critically: "AgentCore is invoke-only — no public HTTP routes, no background poll loop." The public-facing surface is entirely Layer B, which YOU host. First AgentCore deploy ~4–6 minutes; later deploys use cached resources. Other deploy verbs: `package`, `status`, `destroy`, `logs`.

findings.claim: The HTTP contract is CUSTOM (`/apex/*`), not A2A AgentCard, not /.well-known.
findings.detail: The deployed Layer B service exposes `POST /apex/negotiate` and a health route (`/apex/health`, with `/apex/status` also referenced). Negotiate request: `{"task_description": str, "terms": {"deliverables": str, "quality_standards": str}}`. Response: `{"accepted": bool, "price": "<raw uint256 string>", "currency": "<settlement-asset>", "provider_sig": "<EIP-191-signature>", "chain_id": 97, "quote_expires_at": "<5-min-ttl>", "verifying_contract": "<address>"}". Health returns `{"status":"ok","service":"erc8183-service (keyless)","keyless":true}`. The registered ERC-8004 endpoint is the `/apex/` base path, e.g. `bag erc8004 register --endpoint https://my-service.example.com/apex/`. NO `.well-known` JSON is mentioned anywhere in the docs; no A2A AgentCard schema is defined. ERC-8183 is invoked by name ("ERC-8183 Client", "ERC-8183 workflows", `[payments.erc8183]`) but the docs do not publish its wire schema — the `/apex/*` shape above is the observable contract. AiKi should treat `/apex/negotiate` as the integration point and must obtain the base URL from the on-chain `agentURI`.

findings.claim: Agent wallet: user-custodied keystore; spend caps and EIP-712 allowlists are enforced OFF-CHAIN, in-process.
findings.detail: "Private keys live only in user-controlled environments — the keystore never leaves your Agent via public channels." Keystore at workspace root `.studio/wallets/`, deliberately outside the AgentCore code dir so it is not packaged into deploy artifacts; injected at runtime from AWS Secrets Manager as `WALLET_KEYSTORE_JSON`. `WALLET_PASSWORD` is never persisted to config. Policy enforcement lives in `app/agent/signing.py` (fixed, non-LLM code): it clamps prices to `[min_price, max_price]` from `studio.toml` `[payments.erc8183]` before submission and re-validates chain state before every submission. Default EIP-712 allowlist: EIP-3009 `TransferWithAuthorization` and `ReceiveWithAuthorization` PERMITTED; ERC-2612 `Permit` and Permit2 variants DENIED by default. Extend via `[wallet.signing]` `extra_domains` / `extra_primary_types`. This is entirely off-chain/in-process — there is no smart-account, session-key contract, or on-chain spend-cap module described. Security implication for AiKi: a compromised Studio agent process has unbounded on-chain authority; the caps are advisory to that process only, not enforceable by a counterparty.

findings.claim: Trust boundaries: MCP server is read-only (15 tools), Layer B service is keyless, only Layer A can sign.
findings.detail: Documented boundaries: (1) the bundled MCP server for Cursor/Claude Code exposes 15 chain tools and "all 15 tools are read-only — no signing, no on-chain state change"; (2) the Layer B service is keyless — it "can only *request* signatures, never sign directly", via AWS `InvokeAgentRuntime` into Layer A; (3) the keystore is kept outside the AgentCore codebase to prevent accidental packaging. The signing policy lives in fixed code rather than in LLM-reachable surface. Notably ABSENT from the security page: any API-key model, authentication scheme for `/apex/negotiate`, or rate limiting. The negotiate endpoint as documented appears unauthenticated, with replay/abuse control resting on the 5-minute `quote_expires_at` TTL and the `provider_sig`. AiKi should assume it must supply its own authN/rate limiting when calling or when accepting calls from Studio agents.

findings.claim: LLM access is via a gateway ('pieverse-llm') with agent-wallet-funded billing topped up over x402.
findings.detail: `bag init --llm-provider pieverse-llm` is the documented default; quickstart says it "Activates the Pieverse LLM with a $0 deposit (default provider)". Config section is `[llm.pieverse]` holding a `key_hash` and provider config — i.e. a hashed key reference, consistent with a gateway rather than direct provider SDK calls. The `bag llm` command group is `test | activate | status [--full] | topup | allocate | rotate | list-models | usage` — `topup`, `allocate`, `rotate` and `usage` are gateway/credit-accounting verbs, not direct-API verbs. The launch blog states: "Agents pay their own LLM bills from a wallet you fund. They top up automatically via the x402 protocol." No concrete model IDs, context windows, per-token prices, or provider identities are published in any page I fetched — `bag llm list-models` is the runtime source of truth. AWS Free Tier gives limited-time free deployment (48 hours max), which is deploy credit, not LLM credit.

findings.claim: x402 is first-class: `bag x402 quote|buy` CLI verbs plus automatic LLM top-up. No 'b402' term appears anywhere.
findings.detail: The CLI exposes an `x402` command group with `quote` and `buy`. The launch blog states agents "top up automatically via the x402 protocol" for LLM bills. The bnbagent-sdk README references "delegated x402" with a TWAKProvider wallet and a "session-key x402 payer" with AltanaWalletProvider — i.e. the SDK has a WalletProvider seam letting x402 payment authority be delegated or scoped to a session key, with details deferred to wallet-specific READMEs I did not fetch. I saw NO occurrence of the term 'b402' in any fetched BNB source; do not assume Agent Studio speaks a b402 variant. Settlement inside ERC-8183 flows uses EIP-3009 `TransferWithAuthorization`/`ReceiveWithAuthorization` (the default signing allowlist), which is the same primitive x402 uses for stablecoin pulls — so an AiKi facilitator built on EIP-3009 should be wire-compatible with the Studio agent's permitted signing surface.

findings.claim: ERC-8004 registration is OPT-IN and manual, via an explicit CLI step — not automatic on deploy.
findings.detail: Identity is written by running `bag erc8004 register --endpoint https://my-service.example.com/apex/` as a discrete step in the deployment guide, after Layer B is reachable. Because the EC2 IP is not known at scaffold time, the docs show registering a placeholder then correcting it: `bag erc8004 update --new-uri <real-url>` (the CLI reference lists the verb as `update-endpoint`; `show` and `resolve` also exist). This means a meaningful fraction of Studio agents will exist WITHOUT an on-chain record, and some registered records will point at stale or private URLs (the demo literally shows `http://<ec2-ip>:8003/apex`). Registration is described elsewhere as gas-free on BSC Testnet via MegaFuel paymaster sponsorship (low confidence — search snippet, not a fetched primary page). Consequence for AiKi: on-chain enumeration undercounts the true Studio population and will contain dead endpoints; liveness probing `/apex/health` is mandatory before listing an agent.

findings.claim: Package names and install: `bnbagent-studio` (CLI/runtime), `bnbagent-studio-core` (runtime lib), `bnbagent` (SDK). No version numbers published.
findings.detail: PyPI: `bnbagent-studio` provides the `bag` CLI and runtime; `bnbagent-studio-core` is the runtime library supplying wallet, ERC-8004/8183, x402 and signing-policy functionality; `bnbagent` is the standalone BNB Agent SDK (`pip install bnbagent`), with an npm counterpart named `@bnbagent/sdk`. Install: `pip install bnbagent-studio` or `uv tool install bnbagent-studio`. Repos: github.com/bnb-chain/bnbagent-studio and github.com/bnb-chain/bnbagent-sdk. NO version string appeared on any page I fetched — neither the docs index nor the SDK README surfaced one, and `bag --version` is the documented way to check. The SDK README describes ERC-8004 (Agent Identity) and ERC-8183 (Agentic Commerce, "a three-layer stack: AgenticCommerce kernel + EvaluatorRouter + OptimisticPolicy") plus a WalletProvider seam over `sign.message` / `sign.transaction` / `sign.typed_data`. Concrete Python class names were not enumerated in the README excerpt returned.

findings.claim: `bag agents list|show|forget|register` is almost certainly a LOCAL address book, not a network registry query.
findings.detail: The CLI reference groups these under "agents (registry)". The presence of `forget` — a verb that only makes sense against local persisted state, since you cannot un-know a public registry entry — plus the total absence of any network endpoint, base URL or auth for it across every doc page, indicates a client-side cache of counterparty agents the developer has interacted with. It is separate from the `erc8004` group, which is the on-chain identity group. I did NOT fetch a page documenting `bag agents` semantics directly, so this is inference from naming and from the negative evidence of no documented service. AiKi MUST NOT plan launch supply around `bag agents list` returning a global population. Verify by running `bag agents list --help` and inspecting the workspace/`~/.studio` state directory.

findings.claim: Chain IDs: BSC Mainnet 56 and BSC Testnet 97 are both supported; Studio defaults to testnet and demo payloads carry chain_id 97.
findings.detail: The bnbagent-sdk networks page lists exactly two networks: BSC Testnet (97) and BSC Mainnet (56). `bag init` defaults to `--network bsc-testnet`, and agent `studio.toml` carries `[network] default = "bsc-testnet"`. The demo's negotiate response hardcodes `"chain_id": 97`. The BNBAgent SDK is announced as live on BNB Chain mainnet. The networks page explicitly declines to publish deployed contract addresses: "Deployed contract addresses are not listed in this documentation. Use the upstream repositories as the source of truth" — pointing at github.com/bnb-chain/apex-contracts#deployments for ERC-8183/APEX and github.com/bnb-chain/bnbagent-sdk for the ERC-8004 Identity Registry. For AiKi on chain 56, the ERC-8183/APEX settlement contract addresses remain UNVERIFIED and must be read from apex-contracts before any escrow integration.

gaps: EXACT ERC-8004 IdentityRegistry address that `bag erc8004 register` writes to. I have BRC8004's chain-56 address 0xfA09B3397fAC75424422C4D28b1729E3D4f659D7 from the BRC8004 repo README, but NOT confirmation from a bnb-chain primary source that bnbagent-sdk targets it. Resolve by reading constants/config in github.com/bnb-chain/bnbagent-sdk and cross-checking on BscScan.
BSC testnet (97) IdentityRegistry address — not in the BRC8004 README section returned.
ERC-8183 / APEX contract addresses on chain 56. Docs explicitly defer to github.com/bnb-chain/apex-contracts#deployments, which I did not fetch. Required before building escrow/settlement.

The registration event signature and whether IdentityRegistry exposes ERC-721 Enumerable `tokenByIndex`. Only `totalSupply`, `exists`, `getAgentWallet` were confirmed. If IDs are non-sequential or tokens are burnable, a 1..totalSupply() scan breaks — read the ABI directly.
The BNB Chain Agent0 SUBGRAPH_ID on The Graph. The announcement gives only the gateway URL template and says to search 'agent0' in Graph Explorer.
`bag agents list` semantics — local cache vs network call — never documented. Confirm empirically.

The full ERC-8183 wire protocol beyond /apex/negotiate: the paths and payloads for buy / submit / fetch / settle (CLI verbs exist: `bag erc8183 publish|list|status|buy|submit|fetch|settle`) were not published on any page fetched.

The exact JSON schema of the ERC-8004 agent registration file. Field NAMES seen (agent_id, address, name, description, protocol, endpoint, agent_uri) but no verbatim document, no versioning, no confirmation of base64 data-URI vs HTTP vs IPFS hosting in the general case.
Concrete LLM model IDs, per-token pricing, context limits, and the identity of the Pieverse gateway operator. `bag llm list-models` is the only stated source.
AgentCore runtime limits: memory ceiling, request timeout, payload size, cold-start behaviour, concurrency. Docs give only 'first deploy 4–6 minutes'.
Any authentication or rate limiting on POST /apex/negotiate. The security page is silent; the endpoint appears unauthenticated.
Whether 'b402' exists at all in the BNB stack. The term appeared in no fetched source.
Exact package versions for bnbagent-studio / bnbagent-studio-core / bnbagent, and PyPI release dates.
Python class and method names in bnbagent-sdk beyond the sign.message / sign.transaction / sign.typed_data seam and the WalletProvider abstraction.
MegaFuel paymaster gas sponsorship for testnet ERC-8004 registration — seen only in a search snippet, never in a fetched primary page.
Whether ERC-8183 job/offer state itself is enumerable on-chain (would be a second, higher-signal supply source than the identity registry, since it implies an agent is actually selling).
aiki_implications: LAUNCH SUPPLY IS AN INDEXING PROBLEM, NOT AN API-INTEGRATION PROBLEM. Budget for building an ERC-8004 indexer against chain 56 as a launch blocker. There is no BNB endpoint to call. Two implementations: (a) own indexer — poll IdentityRegistry.totalSupply(), fill gaps by scanning ERC-721 Transfer(0x0 -> owner) logs, resolve tokenURI/agentURI per ID; (b) rent The Graph's Agent0 BNB subgraph via gateway API key. Do (b) for week-one supply, ship (a) for control and to avoid a single point of failure.

VERIFY 0xfA09B3397fAC75424422C4D28b1729E3D4f659D7 ON BSCSCAN BEFORE WRITING A LINE OF INDEXER CODE. Read the deployed ABI, confirm it is what bnbagent-sdk writes to, and confirm agent IDs are sequential and non-burnable. If a different registry is in play you will index an empty or wrong set. This is the single highest-leverage unknown in this report.

ENUMERATION GIVES YOU CANDIDATES, NOT INVENTORY. Registration is a manual opt-in step run after deployment, and the docs themselves demo registering a raw `http://<ec2-ip>:8003/apex` URL. Expect stale, private, and plain-HTTP endpoints in the registry. Make a `GET {base}/apex/health` liveness probe (expect `{"status":"ok","keyless":true}`) a hard gate for listing, with periodic re-probing and automatic delisting. This health route is a free, unauthenticated, cheap Studio-agent fingerprint — use it to tag which registry entries are Studio-built.

THE SUPPLY GAP IS AIKI'S OPENING. Studio ships no directory; BNB explicitly leaves discovery to standards. A working directory with liveness, pricing and reputation over chain-56 ERC-8004 is unclaimed surface, not a me-too build. Corollary risk: BNB could ship one, so speed matters and differentiation should sit in trust/execution, not in the listing itself.

BUILD THE /apex/ ADAPTER AS A FIRST-CLASS CONNECTOR. `POST /apex/negotiate` with {task_description, terms{deliverables, quality_standards}} returning {accepted, price, currency, provider_sig, chain_id, quote_expires_at, verifying_contract} is a concrete, implementable contract you can code against today. Treat `provider_sig` (EIP-191) as a verifiable price commitment — recover the signer and check it equals IdentityRegistry.getAgentWallet(agentId). That single check ties an HTTP quote to an on-chain identity and is the cheapest real trust primitive available.

HONOUR THE 5-MINUTE QUOTE TTL IN YOUR STATE MACHINE. `quote_expires_at` is a 5-minute window. Any AiKi flow that caches quotes, batches, or inserts human approval must re-quote rather than replay. Design for quote-refresh, not quote-storage.

DO NOT BUILD FOR AN A2A AGENTCARD OR /.well-known ON THIS STACK. Neither exists in Agent Studio. If AiKi wants AgentCard-shaped metadata, AiKi must synthesise it from the on-chain agentURI JSON (name, description, protocol, endpoint) and publish it itself. That synthesis is a differentiator — position AiKi as the layer that makes BNB agents A2A-legible.

TREAT STUDIO SPEND CAPS AS ZERO ASSURANCE. min_price/max_price clamping lives in `app/agent/signing.py` inside the agent's own process; there is no on-chain smart-account, session key contract, or spend module. A counterparty cannot rely on them. AiKi's escrow/settlement must assume the agent wallet has unbounded authority and must derive safety from the contract side (escrow, optimistic dispute windows) — which is precisely the gap AiKi's trust layer fills.

EIP-3009 IS THE INTEROP KEY. Studio's default signing allowlist permits TransferWithAuthorization and ReceiveWithAuthorization and DENIES ERC-2612 Permit and Permit2. If AiKi's payment rail uses Permit/Permit2, a stock Studio agent will refuse to sign and integration silently fails. Build settlement on EIP-3009, or document the exact `[wallet.signing] extra_domains` / `extra_primary_types` entries an operator must add.

INHERIT THE TWO-LAYER TRUST MODEL RATHER THAN FIGHTING IT. Layer A (AgentCore) is invoke-only with the keys; Layer B is keyless and public-facing. Any AiKi execution component intended to run alongside a Studio agent should sit at Layer B and request signatures, never hold the keystore. This matches the documented boundary and keeps AiKi out of the custody blast radius.

THE NEGOTIATE ENDPOINT IS UNAUTHENTICATED AND UNRATE-LIMITED AS DOCUMENTED. AiKi's crawler will be probing endpoints that have no abuse controls — throttle aggressively and self-identify, or you will be the DoS. Conversely, offering a managed rate-limit/auth shim in front of Studio services is a natural AiKi product wedge.

AGENTS ARE PRICE-QUOTING IN RAW 18-DECIMAL UINT256 STRINGS (e.g. "100000000000000000"). Never parse these as JS numbers. Also note the demo returns `"currency": "<settlement-asset>"` — the settlement token is per-agent and unresolved in docs, so AiKi must handle heterogeneous settlement assets on chain 56 from day one rather than assuming a single stablecoin.

PLAN FOR A TESTNET-HEAVY POPULATION AT LAUNCH. Studio defaults to `--network bsc-testnet` and the demo payloads carry chain_id 97. Real chain-56 supply may be thin initially. Index both 56 and 97, but surface only 56 in production listings — and use the 97 population as an early leading indicator of who is about to go live.

interfaces.name: ERC-8004 agent registration file — field names observed (schema NOT published verbatim)
interfaces.body:
Fields named in the demo page:
  agent_id, address, name, description, protocol, endpoint, agent_uri

Storage: the registry stores agent_uri as base64-encoded JSON (data URI)
containing the Service endpoint, e.g.  http://<ec2-ip>:8003/apex

NO .well-known route. NO A2A AgentCard schema. This is a paraphrase of field
names from prose, NOT a verbatim schema document — treat as unverified until
an on-chain tokenURI is decoded directly.

interfaces.name: Signing policy defaults (enforced in-process, app/agent/signing.py)
interfaces.body:
ALLOWED by default (EIP-712 primary types):
  EIP-3009  TransferWithAuthorization
  EIP-3009  ReceiveWithAuthorization

DENIED by default:
  ERC-2612  Permit
  Permit2   (all variants)

Extend via studio.toml:
  [wallet.signing]
  extra_domains       = [...]
  extra_primary_types = [...]

Price clamp: transaction price forced into [min_price, max_price] from
[payments.erc8183] before submission; chain state re-validated before every
submission. ENFORCEMENT IS OFF-CHAIN / IN-PROCESS ONLY.

Key custody: keystore at .studio/wallets/ (workspace root, outside AgentCore
code dir); injected in prod from AWS Secrets Manager as WALLET_KEYSTORE_JSON.
WALLET_PASSWORD never persisted to config.
